objections.problem: Seed 330 jsonb_sets page-content-writer's default_config at the top-level path {workflow,steps,generate_content,config,prompt_template}. A landmine explicitly names page-content-writer as an agent whose generate_content-equivalent prompt can live NESTED inside a loop's sub_workflow (process_sections_loop), where a census/update at ->'workflow'->'steps' misses it entirely. The plan never verifies the actual live path before targeting it — if the real step is loop-nested, this seed silently writes to a location nothing reads, and the whole consumption half (the stated point of this round) does nothing while reading as applied.

Same top-level-path risk applies to seed 328's target {workflow,steps,plan_sections,config,section_facts} on page-build-handler — not verified against the possibility that plan_sections runs inside a sub_workflow rather than at the top level.

A separate landmine states four agent types carry TWO active default_config rows and only the higher version is ever loaded. Seeds 328/330 update by `type` (per the sketch) without stated confirmation they target the max-version active row for page-content-writer / page-build-handler; if not, the live row is untouched and the seed reports success against a row nobody loads.

Seed 333 is listed as a plan 'edit' with operation config_change but is stated as already applied and live — it changes nothing now. Including a no-op as an edit item (vs. citing it only in grounded_in) blurs edit-count/minimality accounting even though it's clearly disclosed.

reviews.notes: Core mechanism coverage is sound: the carry (1,2), the counter fix (3), durable miss logging (4), and the prompt/wiring seeds (5,7,8) each map to a mechanism the diagnosis names, and none are audit-only no-ops. The mutation-testing and ordering evidence in grounded_in is a genuine strength. My objections are about whether the two held seeds (328, 330) actually land on the live, loaded config path — two landmines in the footprint list warn of exactly this failure mode for these two agent types, and the plan's own risk section doesn't address either, only the object-form-escaping-the-window risk and the counter-meaning risk. These are fixable by adding a pre-apply anchor check (the plan already does this style of check for seed 362's dry run) rather than by redesigning the round.

objections.problem: carrySectionFactsOntoRealised's loop skips any proposed section entry whose 'facts' key is absent or not an array WITHOUT adding it to `pending` at all — so it never appears in the `unmatched` list and never reaches recordFactCarryMisses/FACT_CARRY_UNMATCHED_SECTION. Seed 333 makes the facts key mandatory on every section; a planner emission that omits it (or emits a malformed value) is exactly the disobedience this round's whole measurement strategy depends on catching, yet it is silently indistinguishable from a page correctly emitting no facts. This is the pattern's core shape: required-but-missing data dropped with no error, no warning, on a rebuild/reconcile path — inside code whose stated purpose is to make that class of loss visible.

sameSectionList now compares only section NAME by position, not the full entry — matching the author's own stated fix intent, but this means any page where names line up positionally while other structural aspects differ (e.g. duplicate names in different order-sensitive slots) will be treated as unchanged and skip the carry path entirely, relying entirely on the same name-based identity that RFC_016 s1a already flagged as fragile (per bugs_open/214, a sibling of this exact mechanism on the imagery wire). Worth confirming the council has seen this exact fragile-identity tradeoff before making it a fleet-wide default.

missing: Whether any OTHER rebuild/rerender path that reads plan_sections-produced facts_scoped (e.g. rerender_single_page_action.go, save_page_sections_action.go, rerender_page_sections) shares the same silent-drop exposure this round fixes only inside reconcilePlanWithRealised — the plan does not claim to have audited sibling call sites, and the known pattern (Go template missingkey=zero, case 7) is exactly 'one guarded call site, mechanism generic elsewhere.'
reviews.notes: This plan is unusually pattern-literate: it names the exact silent-drop shape (name match producing an indistinguishable plan whether the carry worked or not), builds a durable agent_error_log guard for it, mutation-tests the guard, and pins all 15 preexisting reconcile tests. That is the proven fix shape from this platform's history (fail loud via a durable record, not a log line) and it is reused correctly here. My objections are about completeness of that same guard (one input-shape gap in the miss-counting) and about whether the fix's scope (one function) leaves sibling rebuild paths with the same exposure — this is architecture-relevant given how many landmines in this index concern exactly this file and exactly this RFC saga; a human should confirm no other consumer of facts_scoped needs the same carry-or-record treatment before this ships broadly.

objections.problem: carrySectionFactsOntoRealised hand-rolls a queue-per-name reattachment across two structurally-divergent lists. The plan's own risks/grounded_in name a sibling defect on the same general problem (site_plan_imagery.scope_ref orphaning, bugs_open/214, landmine-documented) and explicitly declines to unify, calling it 'same wire, different field.' That may be the right call for this round, but no shared 'reattach-by-identity across a restructured list' helper appears to have been searched for before writing a second bespoke implementation of the same shape of fix.

reviews.notes: This plan shows unusually strong reuse discipline for the pieces that matter most: it routes misses through the existing agent_error_log/LogActionError channel (reusing the FACT_SCOPING_EMPTY_COMPOSITION pattern rather than inventing a new artefact kind or table), it reuses sectionEntryName and composeWriterBlock rather than rewriting them, and it explicitly reads the caller ordering rather than assuming it. No new table, migration, or action is added — only two new Go functions plus config/prompt seeds. The one open thread is that the plan itself surfaces a same-shaped defect elsewhere (imagery scope_ref matching) and consciously defers unifying it; that is a reasonable scoping call but worth a human eye per the tool-creation precedent (two paths solving overlapping problems, never unified) named in this seat's brief.

No violation found against the five seat rules: no DDL (no RENAME/DROP COLUMN), no site_work_items writes (dedup/provenance rules N/A), no orchestrator/spawn_agent concerns (all changes are in-process Go actions + prompt/config seeds, not new heavy inline work), and no content_components input_schema required:true/on_missing changes. The section_facts/facts_scoped wiring is step-internal config feeding an action/prompt within a single agent's own workflow, not a cross-agent input_mapping, so DECLARED CONTRACTS (input_contract) does not clearly apply — flagged instead as an input_fields risk via the checks tier, since that's the documented failure mode for prompt template variables, not this seat's hard rule. Commendable: the plan itself identifies and fixes the exact sameSectionList/%v landmine already on file, and stages the DDL-free two-phase-style caution (HOLD suffixes, opt-in keys, mutation tests) consistent with the platform's stated risk posture even though no schema rule was directly in play here.

objections.problem: Seed migrations (328/330/333/362) follow the sql_for_agents/NNN_*.sql convention and cite dry-run verification, but the plan never shows the numbers being claimed against schema_migrations/the ledger before use — the platform's own landmine on this exact pattern warns a migration number is only yours when the ledger says so, not because a file was named. Not blocking since apply order/HOLD gating is otherwise well-documented, but worth a ledger check before 362/328/330 apply.

This round is extensively grounded in prior decisions (RFC_016, corr IDs, owner rulings, guardian veto) via narrative citation, but no edit explicitly writes a doc_notes/doc_plans entry recording this round's decision (the carry mechanism, the sameSectionList fix, the counter-meaning correction) for the next lane to build on — the travelling-docs convention asks for both the load and the leave-behind.

missing: Whether bugs_open/151 / RFC_016 tracking lives in doc_notes rows or only as markdown files under docs/agent_docs — if the former, this round should file a note there; unconfirmed from schema alone.
reviews.notes: No cmd/bundle-equivalent investigation is being reinvented here — this is a functional fix to already-located code (v3_site_actions.go, reconcilePlanWithRealised, sameSectionList) that the landmine footprint itself confirms is the correct home for this logic, not a filename guess. No action/handler is resolved by filename convention; edits target known symbols directly. SQL seed edits follow the established sql_for_agents/NNN_*.sql HOLD/apply-order/snapshot/verify-block pattern already used across the platform, with unusually strong evidence discipline (mutation-tested Go carry, dry-run-verified seed, pinned pre-existing tests). The plan's 'grounded_in' section functions like a doc_notes load even if not literally sourced from that table. Two low-severity gaps only: ledger-claim evidence for the seed numbers, and no explicit NOTES-write-back step for the next lane.

objections.problem: reconcilePlanWithRealised is explicitly the re-plan preservation guard for EVERY site (not this lane's function) — the blast radius is fleet-wide even though the diff is contained to one file. The 15 pre-existing tests passing unmodified is good evidence, but the safety argument for keeping object-form entries from leaking past validate_plan rests on a 176-line window between two hardcoded line numbers (:3101/:3277) in the SAME function that this edit is modifying. That claim decays the moment either line moves in a future edit, and nothing but a comment and an e2e test enforces it.

carrySectionFactsOntoRealised silently produces an indistinguishable plan whether the name-match works or matches nothing (author's own risk note) — the only durable tell is agent_error_log rows one step downstream. That's an acceptable design given the constraints, but it means this action's correctness is unverifiable from outside the mutation-test suite; flagging so the round is judged with that limit in view, not vetoing over it.

This round touches config_change rows on THREE separate agent pipelines (build-site-planner via 362, page-build-handler via 328, page-content-writer via 330) plus one already-applied seed (333) in a single submission. Each is correctly labeled config_change and names its owning pipeline (satisfies surface-ownership), and the apply order is documented (362→328→330, gated on a human compliance read) — but that ordering dependency is enforced only by a doc header (_HOLD suffix), not by tooling. A partial apply (e.g. 362 lands, 328/330 don't) leaves the planner re-emitting realised sections with no consumer wired — is that state confirmed harmless?

reviews.notes: This is NOT the core-plumbing case (coordinator.go/spawn_actions.go) the stability-preference note warns about — v3_site_actions.go is page-planning logic, not the orchestrator/dispatch core, so I'm not invoking that deflection here. The plan is unusually well-instrumented for blast radius: mutation tests, unmodified pre-existing test suite, an explicit ordering claim about the reconcile/normalise window verified by reading the caller. My objections are containment concerns (window-safety enforcement, cross-pipeline apply-order enforcement), not grounds for veto — nothing here spans many Go packages or rewrites an exported/shared wire contract. Config_change edits correctly name their owning pipelines. Recommend proceeding with the two medium objections addressed (e2e test as the enforced gate, not the comment; confirm partial-apply safety across 362/328/330) rather than blocking.

This plan touches site-planning/content-writer machinery (v3_site_actions.go, page-build-handler, page-content-writer prompts) — not the diagnosis loop (pkg/diagnose, diagnose_* actions, diagnosis_artifacts read-only SQL, sqlguard, error_step config, or pod isolation). None of the six load-bearing disciplines this seat guards are implicated: no verdict/citation logic, no SQL guard layers, no diagnosis persistence/notes, no error_step placement, no token/pod isolation change. Out of scope for this council seat; approving on that basis.

objections.problem: Seed 330 rewrites the page-content-writer's live generation prompt (writer prompt v4) — the exact class of artifact the poisoned-spec lesson concerns. The plan correctly gates this behind a human/compliance read of the committed plaintext before apply, but the plan as submitted does not state that this read explicitly checks for overclaimed-reliability phrasing. The three-way branch (scoped/factless/unscoped) introduces new instructional language about what the writer should say when a section has 'no verified facts' — if that instruction (or the else-branch fallback) is phrased as, or causes the model to render, promises like 'every figure here is verified' or 'fully sourced', that ships an unkeepable accuracy claim on whichever site the prompt reaches first (this round's own acceptance target, fundamentallyai). Require the pre-apply human read to explicitly scan the v4 plaintext for banned_claims-class phrasing (source/verified/accurate/authoritative promise language) in addition to checking the writer_block-equality diff, and require the honest replacement framing if any is found: 'we cite what we can; a citation shows where a figure came from, not that it is correct.' Also flag as a coverage question per the standing directive: confirm whether fundamentallyai (the acceptance-test site) currently carries a banned_claims pattern, since site_specs.evidence_base.banned_claims coverage is fleet-uneven and this round is the first live exercise of the new writer branches on that site.

reviews.notes: Everything else in this plan is backend plan-reconciliation plumbing (fact-assignment carry-through, a counter-meaning bug fix, an error-log channel) with no direct user-facing claim, price, or testimonial generation, and no weakening of any scanner or evidence gate — if anything it tightens fact-to-writer-block binding versus today's site-wide fallback, and the unscoped fallback arm is required to stay byte-identical to current behaviour, which is the correct fail-safe. Seed 333 (object-form-mandatory) is prompt-only editorial discipline about declaring facts explicitly, not an invitation to invent them. The sole surface this seat cares about is the v4 writer prompt text itself (seed 330), which the plan already routes through a human/compliance read before apply — my objection narrows what that read must check, it does not block the mechanism.

objections.problem: The claim '(exactly one live agent wires spec_sections into plan_sections, measured 2026-08-06)' scoping this as a low-blast-radius opt-in key is exactly the shape the landmine on 'agent_definitions.default_config->'workflow'->'steps' · process_sections_loop / any step whose config holds a sub_workflow · page-content-writer' warns about: a census that iterates ->'workflow'->'steps' top-level MISSES loop-nested and sub_workflow-nested steps. If plan_sections or a sibling reader of this key sits inside a sub_workflow/loop on another agent, the 'ONE key on ONE row' safety claim is an undercount and the opt-in's actual footprint is wider than stated.

Mutation testing for carrySectionFactsOntoRealised/reconcilePlanWithRealised was run in platform/orchestration/actions/, the exact package the landmine 'A mutant that BREAKS THE BUILD prints the same FAIL as a mutant that was caught' names. The plan states four mutations were each caught by the right test but never states the mutants still compiled — so some or all of the 'caught' results could be compile failures, not logic being exercised.

The correction to sameSectionList and the reconcileCounts struct refactor are validated by commit + unit/mutation tests, but there is no stated post-deploy pod-grep of the running chassis binary for the new symbols (carrySectionFactsOntoRealised, corrected sameSectionList, FACT_CARRY_UNMATCHED_SECTION logging) once this round ships — per 'a deploy is verified by grepping the RUNNING pod's binary, never git, never the image tag.' Slice A's prior pod-verification (v1.0.1262) does not cover this round's new code.

reviews.notes: Config/prompt-seed discipline here is genuinely good: anchored jsonb_set updates, backups (agent_definitions_bak_328/330), verify blocks proven to FAIL by deliberate mutation, and separate HOLD files gating apply order — this is closer to needle-gate discipline than most submissions reaching this council. sameSectionList fix (edit 3) directly matches a landmine already filed against that exact symbol/bug (151) and the plan cites it correctly, which is a good sign of self-awareness rather than a red flag. No sites.status blast-radius issue, no Mode A/B template surgery here, so (b) and (d) are not engaged. My objections are all about verification rigor (census undercount risk, mutation-test validity, missing pod-grep) rather than the SQL surgery mechanics, which are sound.

Root cause is addressed, not patched around: sameSectionList's %v-comparison defect (the actual cause of assignment loss after seed 333) is fixed by comparing section identity, and the deferred prompt half (seed 362, HELD) is explicitly stated and justified rather than silently skipped, with the Go-side name-carry called out as a 'safety net' pending it. No duplicated machinery is evident -- carrySectionFactsOntoRealised is new consumption logic the plan shows does not already exist (zero-hit census with a positive control), and the reconcileCounts struct refactor is disclosed, not a silent rename. No raw/interpolated SQL is exposed in the sketches; jsonb_set and base64-loaded templates are used deliberately to avoid the \set-quoting landmine. Tone is dense and rhetorically heavy (block-caps emphasis) but stays technical, not promotional -- borderline against the plain-tone rule but not a violation worth blocking on.

This is a plumbing/correctness fix inside the fact-assignment pipeline (planner emission -> validate_plan reconciliation -> writer consumption). It does not touch the classifier's authority, does not encode or default any revenue/site shape, and does not let a downstream agent silently override direction — quite the opposite: it replaces a silent drop (assignments discarded by reconcilePlanWithRealised) with explicit surfacing (FACT_CARRY_UNMATCHED_SECTION durable error rows) when a carry can't land, which is exactly the mark-and-surface behaviour the mission calls for instead of silent substitution. The new writer behaviour (seed 330) is opt-in and structured to fail safe: absence of facts_scoped reproduces today's site-wide block byte-identically, so no site's revenue shape or content strategy is being reshaped by this default. Fact scoping serves engagement/accuracy (per-page relevant facts) without dictating consultancy/tools/affiliate/etc. shape. Sequencing, hold-gates, mutation tests and pinned pre-existing tests show real care not to regress the re-plan preservation guarantee. Mission-neutral to mission-serving; approve.

objections.problem: Plan's central premise ('consumption is genuinely zero today') rests on a query result quoted in grounded_in but not independently re-run by this council; the pattern is directly load-bearing (if any agent already wires facts_scoped/assigned_fact_ids, this round would be duplicating a partially-wired consumer rather than greenfield wiring). Attaching an independent check before merge is cheap insurance.

The %v-comparison bug in sameSectionList and the 'snapped_sections silently changed meaning' claim match an existing LANDMINE entry verbatim (agent_definitions.updated_at / prompt-vs-Go metric family), which corroborates rather than contradicts the plan — flagging only so the router can confirm this landmine is the one being cited and not a coincidental restatement.

missing: No check yet confirming the referenced prior council rounds (corr 8ab18991 bugs_open/215 approval, corr 902a8563 guardian veto, corr 1cb17b11 Slice A r2) actually exist in diagnosis_artifacts with the verdicts quoted — this plan's submittability hinges on those being real and correctly characterized.

No check confirming seed 333 was actually applied as claimed ('ALREADY APPLIED 2026-08-08') vs. still HELD — schema_migrations is not in this council's Schema list so this must be settled via council_report/fix_plan precedent search, not assumed from the author's prose.
reviews.notes: This is an unusually well-evidenced submission for this seat's concern: absence claims (zero consumption, %v-comparison counter bug) are backed by cited measurements/positive controls, and the %v bug matches an existing landmine almost verbatim, which is corroboration rather than a red flag. No clear case of building something already deployed elsewhere, and no bare 'does not exist' assertion driving an unfixable-gap conclusion. My objections are purely about re-verifying the plan's own cited evidence and prior-council precedent independently, per procedure, not about detected falsehoods. Approve, checks are advisory/low.

objections.problem: The 176-line window between reconcile (:3101) and normalise (:3277) where object-form section entries flow through pages.sections is protected by call ordering and an e2e test, not by a type boundary. That is an acceptable interim control given the RFC-approved slice size, but it is a latent trap for the NEXT edit to this function — worth a one-line guard (assert normalise runs before any early return) rather than relying on a test catching a future refactor.

reviews.notes:
ARCHITECTURE_SIGNAL: point_fix | DEFLECTIONS: 1

(a) Forward fitness: the future load is plan-time fact assignment surviving re-plan of already-built pages — exactly the load bugs_open/151 needs and Slice A proved the current design cannot carry (assignments emitted, then discarded wholesale by reconcilePlanWithRealised's restore). The architecture change — teaching a shared, string-typed wire (pages.sections) to carry a temporary object form scoped to one function's internals — is real, but it is not novel: RFC_016 already exists, owner decisions (s1a, s3a, s5.3) already ratified the section-entry rule and the slicing order, and the guardian's round-1 veto (corr 902a8563) was explicitly about BREADTH, not about whether this belonged in an RFC. This submission is the RFC's own mandated next slice, not a shared-mechanism change smuggled in as a fix.

(b) Cost of not changing: quantified by the plan itself — without 1b, the 9 fact-overlap pairs that motivated bug 151 sit entirely on already-built pages (index, capabilities, about) that the consumption path can never reach; the acceptance criterion for the whole feature would be unreachable and undiagnosable. That cost is what this plan closes, so it is not a case of a contained route leaving a defect class reachable.

(c) Point fix or architecture change: reconcilePlanWithRealised is, by the author's own description, 'the re-plan preservation guard for every site' — a shared state machine, and the trigger test's 'staged rollout needed' condition genuinely fires (three HELD seeds, explicit apply order, human compliance gate before 330). But the plan already carries that staging, and it lives inside a single package (platform/orchestration/actions) plus config seeds — not a 3-plus-package coordinated edit. The architecture question was already asked and answered via RFC_016; this is implementation, correctly resubmitted at guardian-mandated scope after round 1.

(d) Deflection count: 1 confirmed from the plan's own text (guardian round-1 veto, corr 902a8563, for breadth). I did not run a DB check to look for earlier RFC_016-related deflections beyond what the plan cites; treat the number as a floor, not a ceiling.
